judgment.rationale: Win+Shift+C works but is reported as a system conflict on Windows 11.
evidence: The chord historically belonged to Cortana/Charms, not current Windows 11.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt covers the stale conflict entry.

proposed_fixes.title: Remove obsolete Win+Shift+C conflict reporting
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A historical system shortcut is matched unconditionally on modern Windows.
plan: Locate the system shortcut catalog and matcher.
Remove or OS-gate the legacy entry.
Add positive and negative conflict tests.
verification: Set Color Picker to Win+Shift+C on Windows 11 and confirm no warning while activation still works.

confidence.rationale: Behavior isolates the catalog, but the exact entry needs source confirmation.

issue_context.summary: Color Picker's Win+Shift+C activation works, but Settings shows a misleading system conflict.
known_information: Reporter confirmed the warning after upgrading.
The linked current shortcut page has no matching chord.
inferences: The source is likely stale conflict metadata, not hotkey registration.
The fix must preserve genuine conflicts.
issue_context.analysis: Only the warning is wrong, so investigation should focus on conflict metadata and OS applicability.
initial_investigation: Relevant areas are Settings.UI Helpers/HotkeyConflictHelper.cs and Services/GlobalHotkeyConflictManager.cs.
No linked PR or fork fix exists.

design.root_cause: A legacy Win+Shift+C system mapping is treated as active on Windows 11.
evidence: Inferred: static catalog lacks OS gating.

affected_files.purpose: Matches configured hotkeys against system conflicts.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Matches the legacy chord whenever configured.
implementation_steps.change: Filter the catalog by supported OS applicability before exact chord matching.
implementation_steps.code_block:
var active = GetSystemShortcuts().Where(x => x.IsActiveOnCurrentWindows());
+return active.Any(x => x.Hotkey == candidate);
edge_cases: Do not conflate Win+C or Win+Ctrl+C.
Use a safe baseline if OS version lookup fails.
tests: Unit-test Win+Shift+C exclusion and a known active conflict.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Publishes helper results without applicability metadata.
implementation_steps.change: Publish only applicable conflicts while preserving module/system classification.
tests: Service test verifies inactive entries do not reach the dashboard.

verify: Build Settings UI with the existing repository build path.
On Windows 11 configure Win+Shift+C and verify zero warning plus working Color Picker.
risks: Older supported Windows versions may still need the historical mapping.
Incorrect normalization could hide real conflicts.
alternatives: Suppress only Color Picker; rejected because the catalog remains wrong.
Change the help link only; rejected because the warning itself is false.
